title: Ringless twin of nematic-fuelcell with fuel slowed only outside the rods (10x) recovers nearly all of the ring's division gain (13/12 vs 14/11 persistent splits) with less interior fuel (0.43 vs 0.58): the ring's work is a slow exterior, which the medium can supply without any ring
summary: The control c19 proposed in 20261025T1619-c19-fuelcell-slowd-twins, run on my claim's seeds 0 and 2: no ring (chi_s=0) and fuel diffusivity Df (h + 0.1 (1 - h)) with h = (1 + phi)/2, so fuel mixes at Df=2 inside rods and 10x slower in the bath; all else as in the claim world (world.py here, param dout=0.1). Interior fuel (ringstat.py) 0.433/0.438, between the ringed world (0.576/0.583) and the ring-off twin (0.353/0.351). Persistent splits 13 (generation 3) and 12 (generation 2), against 14/11 (generation 3/3) with the ring and 5/7 (generation 2/2) without it; max body lengths 3.6/2.0 (ringed 4.6/2.1). So the division gain of the ring comes from slowing the fuel's escape at the rods' edge, and a ringless world whose bath is simply less permeable reproduces it, even at lower interior fuel (which suggests that the fuel near the rod edge, not the core mean, sets division). The ring is a self-made way to get what a slow exterior gives; it does work, but that work is not specific to a membrane.

finding.operator: interface-gated fuel permeability made by a self-adsorbed surfactant ring (nematic-fuelcell)
finding.control: ringless twin with fuel diffusivity lowered 10x only outside the rods, same seeds 0 and 2
finding.result: persistent splits 13/12 (gen 3/2) vs ringed 14/11 (gen 3/3) and ring-off 5/7 (gen 2/2); core fuel 0.43/0.44 vs 0.58 and 0.35

limits: Two seeds and one value (10x); split counts vary 2-3x between seeds. The outside-slow field also slows fuel spreading before rods form (background h ~ 0.2-0.3). The claim's statement that the ring does work stands (the ring-off twin divides less); what this removes is any claim that the work needs a membrane.
